newsitem.title: USA: Lomak buys 47 percent of North Coast Energy.
newsitem.headline: Lomak buys 47 percent of North Coast Energy.

text.p: Lomak Petroleum Inc attorney Walter Epstein told Reuters Wednesday the company has bought 47 percent of North Coast Energy Inc shares.

Also on Wednesday Lomak sued North Coast in the Delaware Chancery Courty seeking a court order confirming the election of two Lomak candidates to the North Coast board at that company's annual meeting earlier Wednesday in Twinsburg, Ohio.
The North Coast stake was bought earlier this month from two shareholders who were paid "several million dollars" in cash and oil and gas properties, Epstein said.

"Lomak can enhance the shareholder value (of North Coast) by participating on the board, by growing the company and cutting down expenses." Epstein said. North Coast has a staggered board of six directors.

According to Epstein, the lawsuit was filed after North Coast declared Wednesday's annual meeting adjourned before Lomak could vote its proxies. North Coast alleged an agreement with one of the two previous shareholders prohibited that block of shares being voted against management's slate of directors, Epstein said.
In response to a question on whether Lomak intended to use its stock position to effect a merger, Epstein said "Acquiring more (of North Coast) has not been addressed yet."
However, Epstein said among the savings being considered is a consolidation of Lomak's major administrative operation in Hartville, Ohio, with North Coast's Twinsburg offices.

Lomak, of Fort Worth, Texas, has oil and gas exploration and development operations in the mid-Continent and Appalachia regions of the United States. North Coast is an independent oil and gas exploration operator based in Ohio.

A spokesman for North Coast, Gary Regan, told Reuters the company received the Securities and Exchange Commission 13D document indicating the Lomak share purchase on Tuesday. Regan declined comment on the lawsuit.
